**Not sure which edition?** Take the files above, the standard edition. The files named `Skidbladnir-GPL_…` are the GPL edition: the same app, with x265 writing its HEIC (`-L` lossless, 4:4:4 and 4:2:2 chroma, 10-bit). ### Opening it the first time

Nothing is code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn before they open it.

- **Windows:** SmartScreen says *Windows protected your PC*. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. It installs for your account only, without administrator rights. With Smart App Control turned on, Windows blocks unsigned apps and offers no way past.
- **macOS (experimental):** drag Skidbladnir to Applications and open it. When macOS says it cannot verify the app, close the message, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**. If it says the app is *damaged*, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Skidbladnir.app` in Terminal. CI builds the Mac app and launches it, but nobody has opened it on a real Mac yet, so [Mac reports](https://github.com/basic-automation/Skidbladnir/issues/new/choose) are very welcome.
- **Linux:** `sudo apt install ./Skidbladnir_1.1.0_amd64.deb`, or `chmod +x` the AppImage and run it (it needs FUSE; otherwise run it with `--appimage-extract-and-run`).

### What it is

Each of these formats has an official encoder, and each is a command-line tool with dozens of options. For a still image, every option of `cwebp`, `avifenc` (with libaom), `cjxl` and `heif-enc` (with Kvazaar) is a control in Skidbladnir, labelled with the flag it sets, and Skidbladnir writes the same bytes those tools write, built from the same library versions. CI checks that on every change: **3,665 conversions** run through both the tools and Skidbladnir and must come out identical.

It reads PNG, JPEG (including Photoshop's CMYK), TIFF, WebP, GIF, AVIF, JPEG XL, HEIC, PNM/PAM and PFM; converts animated GIF and WebP to animated WebP; keeps colour profiles, Exif and XMP the way each tool keeps them; and shows the result beside the original before anything is written. Conversion happens on your computer: the app's one network request is the update check at startup.

### Where the claim stops

The README lists the limits under [What "every option" means](https://github.com/basic-automation/Skidbladnir#what-every-option-means). In short:

- **Still images**, plus animated WebP as `img2webp` and `gif2webp` write it. Their `-mixed`, `-min_size`, `-kmin`/`-kmax`, `-loop` and per-frame options are not offered yet, and neither are animated AVIF, JPEG XL or HEIC, or files built from several images.
- **The same encoders, built the same way:** libwebp 1.6.0, libavif 1.4.2 with libaom 3.15.1, libjxl 0.12.0, libheif 1.23.5 with Kvazaar 2.3.2. A packaged `avifenc` usually links libyuv and writes other bytes.
- **Bytes are compared on Linux x86-64.** The Windows and macOS builds link the same sources.
- **TIFF transparency is read correctly by default.** `cwebp` darkens a TIFF with straight alpha, and `heif-enc` one with premultiplied alpha. To get exactly their results, turn on **TIFF input → Read transparency as the official tool does**.
- **The GPL edition's HEIC** is checked by decoding it, not byte for byte.
- Y4M, PGX, EXR and raw-pixel input are not read yet.

### New since 1.0.0

- **TIFF transparency, your choice.** Skidbladnir still reads a semi-transparent TIFF correctly by default. Two official tools misread it: `cwebp` darkens a TIFF with straight alpha, and `heif-enc` one with premultiplied alpha. The new setting **TIFF input → Read transparency as the official tool does** (beside Crop and Resize) reproduces their output byte for byte; with it, there is no `cwebp` or `heif-enc` TIFF result Skidbladnir cannot produce. AVIF and JPEG XL are unaffected (`avifenc` and `cjxl` do not read TIFF). It is off by default and saved with your presets.
- 278 more byte-for-byte comparisons in CI cover it, for **3,665** in all.

### Known gaps

- **Not code-signed** on any platform.
- **macOS is experimental** until a person has run it on a real Mac.
- An AVIF, JPEG XL or HEIC encode cannot be cancelled mid-file.
- No builds for 32-bit systems, Linux on ARM or Windows on ARM.
